Employment Logistics The Sr. Cloud Infrastructure Engineer joins the IT Engineering team during a pivotal phase of the GCP journey. This role will partner closely with the development teams to support the cloud environment shift from manual-heavy operations to a fully automated infrastructure. This individual will help mature the CI/CD environment into a predictable, standardized ecosystem, and lead the effort to standardize Terraform and Ansible playbooks/modules and ensure infrastructure is resilient, scalable, and built on secure guardrails. Unpacking The Benefits Employees are eligible for a comprehensive benefits package which may include: Medical, dental, and vision insurance Life and short- and long-term disability coverage 401(k) retirement savings plan with company match Flex vacation in states other than CA, CO, IL, MA, MT, and NE, with accruals up to 96 hours for first year of employment with tenure-based increases up to 160 hours Two (2) floating holidays per year Paid sick leave* Six (6) paid company holidays Two (2) weeks paid pregnancy disability leave, four (4) weeks paid parental bonding leave Additional wellness and employee assistance programs Benefits eligibility and offerings are subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable plans and company policies. The Must-Haves 5+ years in Cloud Infrastructure & Systems Engineering, with primary expertise in Terraform and IaC Architecture Deep, advanced proficiency with Terraform, including architecting scalable module libraries, state management, environment separation, and establishing code reusable across multi-project environments. Proven experience building, testing, and managing automated IaC pipelines in Azure DevOps (e.g., automated plan/apply workflows, drift detection, static analysis, and policy enforcement). Proficiency with Ansible for configuration management to complement Terraform's provisioning layer. Strong understanding of containerization and orchestration (GKE/Kubernetes vs. VMs) to design scalable, elastic cloud architecture. Strong Linux administration background with a solid command-line foundation for low-level infrastructure debugging. Your Mission In Motion A summary of key responsibilities for the role is outlined below. Additional duties may be assigned as needed to support business objectives. IaC Architecture & Standardization (Terraform): Own and modernize the global Terraform ecosystem—moving away from manual infrastructure changes to dynamic, version-controlled module libraries that eliminate configuration drift. Automated CI/CD for Infrastructure: Build robust Azure DevOps pipelines tailored specifically for infrastructure releases, embedding automated testing, validation, and automated pull-request checks. GCP Cloud Architecture: Partner with engineering teams to design resilient GCP foundations (networking, IAM, database instances) purely defined through code. Technical Mentorship & Governance: Act as the senior voice for IaC standards—establishing code review practices, module documentation, and guiding developers on IaC best practices. Compute & Container Strategy: Help architect the next phase of workloads, evaluating when services should migrate to container orchestration versus managed cloud services or VMs. Reliability & Resilience: Collaborate with teams to define system health, observability, and infrastructure resiliency standards, participating in an on-call rotation to maintain operational availability. Paving Your Way To Your Success You lead the shift from manual work to automation by creating clear standards and driving consistent adoption across teams. You partner effectively with developers to unblock deployments, using strong troubleshooting judgment and a calm, systematic approach. You have the ability to understand application dependencies and troubleshoot build/deployment errors to unblock developers in mixed environments. You balance modernization decisions pragmatically, helping teams choose between containers and VMs based on what each workload needs. Demonstrated experience administering Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) environments in a production setting. Master’s degree in Cybersecurity, Computer Science, Systems Engineering, or a related technical field. Experience with system monitoring, performance metrics, and alerting tools such as Nagios, Zabbix, or Prometheus.
